chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who forgets to shave his head until he departs from Mina, so he said: 'I do not like that he casts off his hair except in Mina, and he has not imposed anything upon him.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And shaving is not sufficient for the completely shorn one except shaving, and for whoever is not completely shorn, trimming is sufficient, and shaving is superior. That is indicated by what he narrated:'

key_terms.تَقْصِير: Trimming (the hair), a less complete form of the ritual act
key_terms.حَلْق: Shaving (the head), a specific ritual act in Hajj
key_terms.صَرْوَرَة: Completely shorn (state of having shaved the head entirely)
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a location near Mecca significant for Hajj rituals

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who forgets to shave his head before leaving Mina during Hajj?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies the juristic distinction between *halq* (complete shaving) and *taqsir* (trimming), establishing shaving as the superior act (*afdhal*) while acknowledging trimming as valid for those unable to shave completely. The Imam’s specific instruction to cast the hair in Mina rather than elsewhere underscores the ritual significance of the location in finalizing the state of *Ihram*. This ruling reflects the Shia emphasis on following the Imams' precise guidance on Hajj rituals to ensure both validity and excellence in worship.
